newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- South Africa's largest trade union federation, COSATU, launches fiery attack on budget procedure in parliament and demands that parliament's finance committee be given powers to amend the budget.

- Malbak Ltd shareholders will be asked on Monday to approve the payment of about 75 million rand to its senior managers as compensation for the effects of a premature termination of the executive share incentive scheme in the wake of the group's unblundling.

- South Africa and Mozambique sign a memorandum of understanding to study the construction of a new hydroelectric project that could open the way for the development of a 1.2 billion rand aluminium smelter near Maputo.
- South Africa's maize crop will be almost two million tonnes smaller than last season, scotching hopes of another bumper harvest and strong exports earnings for the country, official estimates show.

- Top police officers including former police commissioner General Johan van der Merwe covered up the death of ANC-aligned activist Stanza Bopape in 1988 and allegedly fed their minister, Adriaan Vlok, false information which he presented to parliament as the truth.

- South African captains of industry hobnobbed on Thursday night with international celebrities at a gala fundraising banquet on Robben Island hosted by President Nelson Mandela, raising five million rand for the island's museum and for former political prisoners.

- Justice Minister Dullah Omar orders an inquest into the deaths of 19 people during the March 1994 shootings in central Johannesburg. More than 50 people were killed in and around Greater Johannesburg after Zulu loyalists marched through the city centre.
- Ex-Police chief Johan van der Merwe seeks amnesty for covering up the death under police torture of activist Stanza Bopape in 1988.
- President Nelson Mandela shows U.S. First Lady Hillary Clinton and her daughter Chelsea the tiny cell on Robben Island where he spent most of his 27 years as a political prisoner.

- The South African Democratic Teachers' Union demands that Finance Minister Trevor Manuel withdraw his remark that most teachers, while lobbying for higher salaries, spent most of their time in shebeens (township pubs).

- African National Congress chairman in Germiston, east of Johannesburg, Mpendulo Majola resigns saying the party is not prepared to listen to its grassroots members. The branch had been campaigning for the reinstatement of sacked deputy minister Bantu Holomisa.
